title: Soya chunk keema
summary: Soya granules cooked like mutton keema. Around 25 g of protein a serving for pocket change, and the texture genuinely fools people.

ingredients.qty: 1.5 cups granules, or chunks pulsed coarse in a blender

steps: Pour boiling water over the soya with 1/2 tsp salt and leave 15 minutes. Drain, then rinse under cold water and squeeze out every bit of liquid with your hands. This step is not optional - waterlogged soya tastes of nothing and takes up no masala.
Heat the oil, crackle the cumin, then cook the onions properly - 8 minutes, until genuinely brown at the edges, not just soft. This is where the depth comes from.
Ginger and garlic paste for a minute, until the raw smell goes.
Powdered spices and salt with 2 tbsp water, 30 seconds.
Tomatoes in. Cook 6-8 minutes until the mixture thickens and oil beads at the sides.
Add the squeezed soya and peas. Stir to coat, add 1/2 cup water, cover and simmer 8 minutes.
Uncover, cook off any excess liquid - keema should be moist, not soupy. Finish with garam masala, crushed kasuri methi, coriander and lemon.
tips: Squeeze the soya like you mean it. Half the complaints about soya chunks come from skipping this.
Chunks blitzed in a blender give a better keema texture than the granules you buy ready-made.
Goes in a wrap, over rice, or on toast with a fried egg on top.
health_notes: Soya chunks are about 52 g of protein per 100 g dry, which is the highest of any cheap vegetarian staple, and a complete amino acid profile.

source.adapted: Standard mutton keema masala with rehydrated soya standing in for the mince.
